a:r.a:t: Damaged mRNA lead to the formation of an incomplete or peptide and a “nonstop complex.”
The ribosome is rescued by trans-translation.
A transfer-messenger RNA (tmRNA) and small protein B (SmpB) bind to the stalled complex in the empty A site.
Translation continues until a stop codon is found in the tmRNA.
The defective mRNA and polypeptide are both degraded.

p:cNvPr.descr: Bacterial ribosomes rescued by tmRNA. This has the same large and small subunit with the same elongated intertwined green structure, labeled as a stalled ribosome (non-stop complex), but this has one of the green structures in the E column and another in the middle. The one in the middle has three blue balls coming from the top. The mRNA line begins at the bottom left before the image, then travels right horizontally, then angles up and right, and ends just below the second green structure. It originates with 5’. At the right ends, it states, “3’ end lacking stop codon.” Below this is a down arrow with a replicated image, but this one has an elongated orange image like the green structure. This also has a blue circle with Tu, which bonds right to GTP. At the top right is a light blue sphere, labeled as Ala. From the bottom of this structure, an orange line extends down and right, then horizontal. Towards the end is a small red section labeled as “stop.” It ends with 3’. To the right of the image is this same orange image with the extended orange line, labeled as tmRNA. In a box below, it states, “Transfer-messenger RNA (tmRNA) has a 5’ end that mimics tRNA structure, and a 3’ end that acts as a continuation of the mRNA.” Below this is a down arrow with another arrow jutting right to Tu in a blue circle, which bonds right to GDP. Belw this is a replica of the previous image, but the tmRNA only has the small blue sphere, now at the left top. This illustrates transpeptidation adds Ala to peptide chain. Below this is a down arrow indicating translocation and replacement of mRNA rescues stalled ribosome. Below this is another replicated image of the previous image, but this one has the orange image in the middle with the blue sphere above and three blue circles on top of that. The green image on the right has a blue circle on the top left. This image has an arrow pointing right to this same green image with “AA” on top. To the left, the green image has an arrow pointing left to a replica of that same green image. Below that is a down arrow indicating translocation of mRNA reading frame continues to stop codon. Below this is another replicated subunit image. In this one, the middle orange image is now green, with two blue circles on top, followed by a blue sphere, then several more blue circles traveling up then left. The first one above is labeled as AA, then next one as AA, and the blue sphere labeled as Ala. The orange image in the previous image is now at the left of the small subunit with its line extending right horizontally, then turning up and right and travels along the bottom of the three green images and ends on the bottom right of the subunit. To the right, it states, “Stop codon in tmRNA permits normal termination and ribosome recycling.” Below this is a down arrow to a line of blue circles, with the fourth one being a blue sphere. This begins with N, which bonds right to three empty circles, then the blue sphere labeled as Ala, then 9 blue circles, each labeled as AA. The last one bonds right to C. This is labeled as tagged polypeptide. From here, a down arrow points to “Degradation by cellular proteases.”
